results.references:
- B. T. Polyak. [Some methods of speeding up the convergence of iteration methods](https://doi.org/10.1016/0041-5553(64)90137-5). 1964. Complexity: $O(n(L/\mu)\log(LR^2/\varepsilon))$ exact component-gradient calls using the full-gradient method for objective gap at most $\varepsilon$, counting $n$ component calls per iteration; $0<\varepsilon<LR^2/2$.
- James W. Daniel. [The Conjugate Gradient Method for Linear and Nonlinear Operator Equations](https://doi.org/10.1137/0704002). 1967. Complexity: $O(n[1+\sqrt{L/\mu}\log(LR^2/\varepsilon)])$ exact component-gradient calls using conjugate gradients for objective gap at most $\varepsilon$, including initialization and component queries implementing operator products; $0<\varepsilon<LR^2/2$.

problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: Unconstrained minimization of an L-smooth quadratic objective on a complete real Hilbert space. Individual quadratic components may be nonconvex, but their average is convex.

problem_class.label: strongly_convex
problem_class.details: The average operator satisfies ⟨x,(n⁻¹∑ᵢAᵢ)x⟩ ≥ μ‖x‖² for every x, so the objective is μ-strongly convex. Parameters satisfy 0<μ≤L.

problem_class.label: finite_sum
problem_class.details: f(x)=n⁻¹∑ᵢ[⟨x,Aᵢx⟩/2+⟨bᵢ,x⟩], with n≥1. Each Aᵢ is a bounded symmetric linear operator with ‖Aᵢ‖≤L.

oracle.label: component_gradient
oracle.details: A query chooses any component i and point x and returns exactly Aᵢx+bᵢ. Replies have no error, noise, or dependence on call index or seed. All Params, including n,L,μ,R,G,ε,x0 and the ambient space, are public; Aᵢ and bᵢ are hidden. Oracle budgets count individual component queries and are fixed for every seed.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/QuadraticFiniteSum.lean: spec.Public, spec.publicInput, spec.Query, spec.admissible; LongTails/Template.lean: execute and Convergence.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: Quadratic components may have indefinite Hessians; only their average must be positive definite. A minimizer x⋆ exists with ∑ᵢ(Aᵢx⋆+bᵢ)=0, ‖x0−x⋆‖≤R, and maxᵢ‖Aᵢx⋆+bᵢ‖≤G, where R,G≥0 are public. The gradient bound holds at the minimizer, not globally. No finite-dimensionality or separability assumption is imposed.

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: Return a measurable Hilbert-space-valued output X whose objective gap relative to a global minimizer is integrable and satisfies E[f(X)−f(x⋆)]≤ε, with ε>0. No particular iterate or averaging rule is required.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: The guarantee is an expectation under the product of the algorithm and oracle seed laws. Algorithmic randomization is permitted despite exact oracle replies.
accuracy.evidence: LongTails/Setups/QuadraticFiniteSum.lean: spec.successful; LongTails/Template.lean: Algorithm.law, Oracle.law, Convergence.

setup_category.label: classical
setup_category.reason: Strongly convex quadratic finite-sum minimization with exact component gradients, an initial-distance bound, and expected objective-gap accuracy is an established optimization formulation, including variants permitting nonconvex components.
